blocks.text: A complex ion has a central metal ion bonded to surrounding electron-donating species. The metal ion acts as a Lewis acid (electron-pair acceptor) and molecules or ions with lone pairs, such as H2O, NH3, Cl- and OH-, act as Lewis bases. The number of coordinate bonds to the metal ion is the coordination number; common values are 2, 4 and 6.

Complex formation is more typical of transition metals, which have available d orbitals, but Group 2 ions can also form complexes, especially those at the top of the group. Smaller ions have a higher charge density and attract donor species better, and all Group 2 ions carry a +2 charge.

blocks.long_description: A complex ion has a central metal ion bonded to electron-pair donors (ligands) by coordinate bonds; the number of such bonds is the coordination number. Group 2 ions form complexes less readily than transition-metal ions, the smaller ions most easily. In water the ions are hydrated: Be2+ forms [Be(H2O)4]2+ (coordination number 4) and Mg2+ forms the octahedral [Mg(H2O)6]2+ (coordination number 6). A ligand with several donor atoms can grip one ion from several sides, forming rings: EDTA uses six donor pairs to hold Ca2+, which is how it softens hard water and removes metal ions from the body.

items: Hydrated ions: when Group 2 salts dissolve, the ions are hydrated, water acting as the electron-pair donor. Be2+, the smallest, forms [Be(H2O)4]2+ (coordination number 4); Mg2+ forms [Mg(H2O)6]2+ (coordination number 6); Ca2+, Sr2+ and Ba2+ also mostly have coordination number 6, with weaker interaction down the group.

Chelates: ions, especially the smaller ones, form stable complexes with donors that have more than one donor pair, which make several bonds to the same ion and form rings. Ca2+ forms a ring complex with EDTA (ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid), a six-pair donor: Ca2+ + EDTA4- -> [Ca(EDTA)]2-. EDTA is used to soften water by removing Ca2+ and Mg2+, and in medicine to remove toxic metal ions from the body.

blocks.prompt: Why does MgSO4 dissolve more easily than BaSO4?
blocks.explanation: The small Mg2+ ion has a much more negative hydration enthalpy, while the lattice enthalpy of the sulphates, with their large anion, changes little; so the energy balance favours dissolving MgSO4 but not BaSO4.

items: Complex ion: central metal ion + ligands; coordination number = number of coordinate bonds.
